query: Taking nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 as the starting material, what single intervention could prevent its radiation-induced precipitation while retaining its negligible irradiation hardening and improving its suitability for practical bulk fabrication? Formulate one testable hypothesis for energetic-particle irradiation relevant to fusion service, including comparison with the unmodified alloy at approximately 8 dpa; identify the intervention and mechanism, predict quantitative or directional changes in precipitation, irradiation defects, and hardening, define the applicable irradiation and thermal boundaries, cite supporting prior evidence, and propose a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 1 at.% Ti and 0.5 at.% C to nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11, followed by annealing at 800°C for 1 hour, will reduce radiation-induced precipitation and retain negligible irradiation hardening, while improving the alloy's thermal stability and suitability for practical bulk fabrication.
generation.intervention: Addition of 1 at.% Ti and 0.5 at.% C, followed by annealing at 800°C for 1 hour
generation.conditions: Irradiation with 5 MeV Fe ions at 500°C to 10 dpa
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary segregation and precipitation of TiC
generation.mechanism: TiC precipitation at grain boundaries reduces radiation-induced precipitation of other phases, while Ti and C solutes enhance grain boundary cohesion and reduce irradiation-induced defect formation
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduced radiation-induced precipitation, retained negligible irradiation hardening, and improved thermal stability compared to the unmodified alloy
generation.uncertainty: The effect of the Ti and C addition on the alloy's irradiation hardening and thermal stability, and the optimization of the annealing conditions
